answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table: memory_b1's success is irrelevant here because compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the strongest-looking precedent cannot be used. That leaves the region-confined write-path degradation. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the most direct match to 'confined to the primary region' and is why I want its source record — but b2 was a latency degradation of unstated write intensity, and a cross-region cutover executed at peak settlement write volume is precisely the condition where replication lag is largest, so the failure mode is losing in-flight customer writes. That collides head-on with the stated objective ('without losing customer writes'), so I am flagging it rather than treating b2 as transferable. Routing report/dashboard queries to read replicas (memory_b5) is the intervention whose recorded outcome is specifically transactional write-latency recovery, and it carries no write-loss path: it sheds read load off the primary and is trivially reversible. I want b5's source record to check whether the recovery was actually attributable to read offload and whether the primary was contended the same way it is now, or whether it was a slow dashboard problem that happened to coincide. add_capacity (b3) was pre-provisioned ahead of a known peak, not applied 90 minutes into an active climb, so it likely will not land in time. Circuit breakers (b4) contained an external partner failure; here the primary itself is the degraded component, so failing fast would shed the customer writes we are trying to preserve. Choosing standard_experiment rather than broad rollout: I do not yet know the cause of the climb, and if b5's verified record does not support read contention as the mechanism, I should escalate to a staged failover in the next window rather than have committed the whole platform to a mechanism that only matched by analogy. Real uncertainty remains about root cause.
